prize_parts.citation: For the development of general, ligand-controlled palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I have not changed my preferred configuration after round 1. I keep palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling as the whole prize. The case is mechanistic: the reaction needed its own solution to amine binding, base-mediated deprotonation, and competition from beta-hydride elimination, and that solution came from ligand design that controls oxidative addition, amine coordination and reductive elimination. Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general method independently and in parallel, with complementary ligand families, so two names describe the credit completely. About three decades of independent confirmation and daily use in drug, agrochemical and materials synthesis mean there is no maturity question. It is the only configuration on the table that is mature, mechanistically clean and cleanly attributable at the same time.
statement.case_against: The 2010 cross-coupling prize is the real cost. A skeptical member can say that C-N coupling extends a recognised catalytic cycle to a new nucleophile, and I can state the difference in one sentence only if the citation says 'general, ligand-controlled', which makes the prize about the ligand logic and not about the reaction class. Excluding Kosugi, Migita, Guram and Rennels rests on generality, and I recall that history without having verified it. By contrast B014 offers a new pharmacological principle, and if its credit could be drawn cleanly, the novelty argument would favour it.

responses.point: Aili now puts Handa in the third place of B014 so that the PROTAC concept is joined to the cereblon mechanism of drugs that already help patients, and treats this as answering the clinical-validation worry.
responses.response: I follow the logic, but I think it answers the maturity question by changing the achievement. Cereblon as the target of thalidomide-class drugs is a mechanism discovery that was clinically validated before PROTACs existed, so it does not validate the heterobifunctional strand. Placing Handa beside Crews and Deshaies also leaves out Ito, who shares the cereblon paper, and Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto. The citation would be forced to name two different achievements with three people. If the committee wants B014, I would rather see it tested as one induced-proximity principle with a candid statement of who is left out, and I do not think that statement is ready yet.

responses.point: Chabes supports Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as concept, structure-guided chemistry and mechanistic rationale, concedes that the cereblon strand is uncredited and that few degraders are approved, and lists B046 as having no maturity question.
responses.response: We agree on the maturity contrast, and I accept that the Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli chain is internally coherent as a PROTAC story. That is the stronger of the two B014 trios as chemistry. My difficulty is that your own file calls the cereblon lineage a distinct glue achievement left out, which means the prize cannot honestly be called 'targeted protein degradation' without a citation that narrows it to PROTACs. A narrowed citation is defensible, but it is a smaller claim than the one the three B014 supporters have been making. I would move to it only if the committee accepts that narrower claim and does not require clinical approval.

responses.point: Somfai argues that Kosugi's stoichiometric tin-amide chemistry lacked scope and should be excluded openly, and that the 2010 overlap depends on how the citation is framed.
responses.response: I agree and take your point about saying so openly. Where I would tighten it is the citation: 'general' and 'ligand-controlled' should both appear, because they are what separates the catalytic amination from Kosugi's tin amides and from the C-C reactions rewarded in 2010. I also think we should not let the committee treat exclusion of Guram and Rennels as settled by our memory. They were contemporaneous with Buchwald, and the committee should record that their contribution was seen and weighed.

responses.point: Linke prefers Car and Parrinello because credit is unambiguous, maturity is four decades, and it does not overlap with recent computational prizes, while conceding the physics flavour and the 2013 and 2024 prizes.
responses.response: Your credit argument is the strongest in the room and I keep B027 as an alternative for that reason. I still rank it behind B046 because the visible effect on what chemists do at the bench is smaller, and a third computational prize in about fifteen years is a real headwind. If B046 fails on the 2010 overlap, then B027 is a cleaner fallback than a B014 split, because it asks the committee to settle nothing about attribution.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that C-N coupling is distinct from the 2010 prize, which depends on a citation emphasising ligand-controlled generality.
Whether excluding Kosugi, Migita, Guram and Rennels will look defensible; my recollection of their precedence is unverified here.
Whether B014 can be narrowed to a PROTAC-only citation that the committee finds acceptable without clinical approval of a degrader.
What evidence would move me: a clean one-sentence statement of the PROTAC and glue strands as one principle with a defensible three-name credit would make B014 a serious competitor.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My profile records a Stockholm University connection to Xiaodong Zou, who also prefers B046, but neither of us is connected with Buchwald, Hartwig or any other candidate. My own research on biological energy conversion is not represented on the shortlist. I did not change my disclosure from round 1.
